prompt: The point $(4, -3)$ is reflected across the $x$-axis. Write the coordinates of the image in the form (x, y).
hint: The $x$-axis is a horizontal mirror, so the point flips up or down but never sideways.

hints.text: The $x$-axis is a horizontal mirror, so the point flips up or down but never sideways.
Keep $x$ the same and change the sign of $y$: $(x, y) \to (x, -y)$.

explanation: Reflecting across the $x$-axis leaves the horizontal position alone and flips the vertical one.
So $(4, -3) \to (4, 3)$ — it was $3$ below the axis, now it is $3$ above.

alternativeExplanations.title: Mirror distance check
steps: The point was $3$ units below the $x$-axis.
A mirror image sits the same distance on the other side, so it must be $3$ units above, still in the same column $x = 4$: $(4, 3)$.
